SEC25A-01.note: Plural 'Cattle' plus present tense set by 'comes' in the proviso clause. 'were safe' attracts through the passage's past-tense opening ('was screened').

SEC25A-02.note: 'Each X and Y' takes a singular verb; past tense from 'recognized'. 'were developing' attracts via the compound subject and plural 'trays' next to the blank.

SEC25A-03.note: Singular head 'comparison' (not 'candidates'); specific past time ('on the third day of that year's monsoon') rules out present perfect. 'were halted' attracts via 'candidates'.

SEC25A-04.note: Elliptical auxiliary must recover 'withstood' from 'has withstood', so present perfect 'have not'; plural 'cultivars'. 'do not' attracts as the natural present-tense negation but cannot recover 'withstood'.

SEC25A-05.convention: pronoun-antecedent agreement: 'their' has a grammatical plural antecedent ('nurses'); possession of the refrigerator is not fixed by the text
SEC25A-05.note: Plural 'nurses' -> 'have moved'; the refrigerator is the clinic's, so 'its'. However 'their' agrees grammatically with 'nurses' and nothing in the text forbids the refrigerator being the outreach nurses' own, so the pronoun half is not decided by agreement.

SEC25A-06.note: Plural 'health workers' -> 'carry'; the thing carried is the single heat-stable cholera vaccine -> 'it'. 'carry them' attracts via 'three oral vaccines'.

SEC25A-07.note: Singular 'Contact dermatitis' with a long appositive interrupter; 'recurred' (5+ words later) is intransitive, so only 'has' forms a grammatical perfect. 'is' attracts as the reader expects a predicate adjective before seeing 'recurred'.

SEC25A-08.note: Restrictive participial phrase (only the samples from that barn were retested; samples came from all four barns) takes no punctuation. 'samples, drawn' attracts as a familiar nonrestrictive shape; D separates participle from its complement.

SEC25B-01.note: Singular 'atlas' (not 'trails'); present tense from 'turns out' in the conditional. 'are revised' attracts via 'trails'.

SEC25B-02.note: Plural 'water mains'; specific past time 'at the height of last winter's cold snap' requires simple past progressive. 'has been losing'/'was losing' attract via 'hospital'/'reservoir'.

SEC25B-03.note: Singular 'seismometer' (not 'aftershocks'); present tense from 'sort out'. 'are being calibrated' attracts via 'aftershocks' adjacent to the blank.

SEC25B-04.note: Plural 'survey teams' -> 'are sampling'; the emissions are the lone active vent's -> 'its'. 'their' attracts by matching 'teams' (or 'craters').

SEC25B-05.note: Elliptical auxiliary recovers 'discharge ... at a nearly constant rate' from the present-tense main clause -> 'does not', singular 'geyser'. 'was not' attracts via the past tense of the next sentence ('came').

SEC25B-06.note: Singular 'glare' (not 'panels'); past tense from 'struck'. 'are dangerous' attracts via 'panels' adjacent.

SEC25B-07.note: Compound subject 'a technician and two engineers' -> 'were'; the object is the single dish -> 'it'. 'was covering' attracts via the singular first conjunct 'a technician'; 'them' via 'wind farms'.

SEC25B-08.note: Two independent clauses ('A landslide ... left a jagged scar' / 'a crescent ... drew climbers') need a semicolon. The colon attracts but the second clause does not explain the first; the comma reads as an appositive until 'drew' arrives, creating a splice.

SEC25C-01.note: Compound subject 'the fresco and the gilded screen'; present tense from 'are moved'. 'is blackening' attracts via 'chancel' adjacent.

SEC25C-02.note: Singular 'rivalry' (not 'bands'); present tense from 'have read out'. 'are reported' attracts via 'bands' adjacent.

SEC25C-03.note: Singular 'portrait' (not 'sisters'); bounded past period 'during the decades after the painters' deaths' -> simple past. 'have been obscure' attracts via 'sisters'.

SEC25C-04.note: Plural 'townspeople' -> 'were'; they defended the porch/cathedral -> 'its'. 'their' attracts by matching 'townspeople'.

SEC25C-05.note: Singular 'restorer' with appositive interrupter -> 'has uncovered'; the object is the frescoes -> 'them'. 'it' attracts via 'apse'/'whitewash' or matching 'restorer'.

SEC25C-06.note: Elliptical predicate recovers 'structurally sound' from the past-tense first clause; plural head 'remains' -> 'were not'. 'was not' attracts via 'tower' adjacent.

SEC25C-07.note: Singular 'chapel' (not 'stalls') -> 'was visited'; the visitors are the choir monks -> 'by them'. 'were visited' attracts via 'stalls'.

SEC25C-08.note: 'Both men' and 'two distinct hands' show two copyists -> plural possessive 'copyists''. 'copyist's' attracts via 'a hired copyist' earlier.

SEC25D-01.note: Elliptical predicate recovers 'eligible' -> 'are not'; 'the elderly' is plural. 'is not' attracts by treating 'the elderly' as singular; 'have not' attracts via 'has registered'.

SEC25D-02.note: Singular 'eye tracker' -> 'follows'; the eyes are the infants' -> 'their'. 'its' attracts by matching 'tracker'.

SEC25D-03.note: A direct question ('which language should the merged school teach') ends with a question mark, and a new sentence begins. The period attracts because the question is embedded after a colon.

SEC25D-04.note: Plural 'applications' (not 'employer'); past tense from 'reached' in the conditional. 'has been routed' attracts via 'employer' adjacent.

SEC25D-05.note: Plural 'berth assignments' (not 'crews'); past tense from 'voted'. 'has been provisional' attracts via the present-tense 'argue' later.

SEC25D-06.note: Singular 'archivist' -> 'is converting'; the tapes are converted -> 'them'. 'it' attracts via 'trunk'/'museum'.

SEC25D-07.note: Singular 'bookkeeper' with long appositive -> 'was entering'; the names are the borrowers' -> 'their'. 'its' attracts by matching 'bookkeeper' or reading 'lender'.

SEC25D-08.note: 'voters never changed mayors' -> one mayor -> singular possessive 'mayor's'. 'mayors'' attracts via the plural 'mayors' in the prior sentence.

tells: Verb+pronoun 2x2 grids (10 items: SEC25A-05, SEC25A-06, SEC25B-04, SEC25B-07, SEC25C-04, SEC25C-05, SEC25C-07, SEC25D-02, SEC25D-06, SEC25D-07): in EVERY one the key pairs the verb with a pronoun of the OPPOSITE number (plural verb + its/it, singular verb + them/their). The two options whose verb and pronoun share a number always lose, so a test-taker who solves only the verb (or only the pronoun) gets the item free, and one who guesses 'mismatched pair' wins 10/10 at a 50% floor.

Present-perfect options (has been / have been) are never the key in the tense x number grids: SEC25A-03, SEC25B-02, SEC25C-03, SEC25D-04, SEC25D-05 all key simple past; SEC25A-01/B-01/B-03/C-01/C-02 key simple present. Eliminating the perfect pair is free.

In the subject-verb items the noun immediately before the blank is almost always the attractor and the key disagrees with it in number (SEC25A-02, A-03, B-01, B-03, B-06, C-01, C-02, C-03, C-06, D-04, D-05): 'disagree with the adjacent noun' picks the number half without finding the subject.
Elliptical items (SEC25A-04, SEC25B-05, SEC25C-06, SEC25D-01) all end the clause with the blank and test auxiliary recovery; once seen, the template is recognisable.
